headline: Cyber Resilience Act takes shape; cobot payback cases get concrete

summary.text: Germany's Bundesrat cleared the national Cyber Resilience Act implementing law, so makers of connected products now face concrete national obligations for cybersecurity and vulnerability reporting.
The first European standard supporting the CRA is published, giving manufacturers a route to presumed conformity, while PwC's overview lays out requirements and timeline for planning.
CBAM rules allow deduction of carbon prices paid in third countries, which can lower costs for importers but only with documented evidence.
An Atlas Copco cobot case reports 10.5 months payback, and ABB's palletizing template cuts cobot palletizing deployment time by up to 80%, easing automation against labour shortage.
Factory AI that tunes machines works best with limits on what it can change, and Siemens links Industrial AI with additive manufacturing; both point to bounded, practical AI entry points.

actions.text: Product and engineering heads: inventory products with digital elements and assign owners for CRA conformity and vulnerability handling; consultants should check the new harmonised standard against that list.
Purchasing and finance: check whether CBAM-covered imports qualify for third-country carbon price deduction and start collecting the required documentary evidence from suppliers.
Production managers: use the 10.5-month payback and ABB's palletizing template as benchmarks to scope one cobot palletizing pilot; consider the Chemnitz workshop for peer exchange.
